cross_gpu.decision: declined with ROG_DOVI_DECLINE_CROSS_DEVICE (2048) until a reference exists
cross_gpu.why: No same-device reference: NVIDIA GBM refuses a linear ABGR2101010 buffer (EINVAL). Against Intel's own 10-bit output on the same picture the cross output differed by at most 1 code for P8.1 PQ (99.291% identical) and P5 PQ (99.9913%), but by up to 5 codes at the SDR destination (93.4641% identical; 46,659 pixels at 3 codes), which is beyond the half-code device rounding known for PQ.

process_exit.backtrace_installed_rogdv12: gdb, two mappers in turn: thread 1 SIGSEGV at an unmapped address called from __run_exit_handlers+495 (stack: __libc_start_call_main -> exit -> __run_exit_handlers -> handler). LD_DEBUG=files: the last library mapped at that address was libEGL_nvidia.so.0 (handler at +0x9fbec), which had been unloaded ('calling fini') when the Vulkan loader released the NVIDIA ICD after the last device was destroyed. libEGL_nvidia imports __cxa_atexit.
process_exit.staged_vs_installed_rate: Same fault, same cause; the lower rate is not a behavioural difference that was found: device release is the same sequence (queued destroy on one worker thread, drained at exit), with a pthread worker in place of a GThreadPool. Treated as timing.
process_exit.fix: One mechanism: the GTK adapter creates its mapper with ROG_DOVI_MAPPER_KEEP_DEVICE, the same flag Firefox uses, so the device and the driver are never unloaded. The explicit-node path additionally keeps its enumeration instance (an instance, not a device) because a non-keep node mapper would otherwise unload the drivers the same way.
process_exit.keep_check: core probe: profile query then mapper on one node creates 2 devices without the flag and 1 with it
